//: EAS build and submit profiles for apps/mobile.
eas build --profile development --platform android   installable dev client
eas build --profile preview     --platform all       internal APK / TestFlight
eas build --profile production  --platform all       store binaries
WHY THE ENV BLOCKS ARE HERE AND NOT IN .env:
Babel inlines every EXPO_PUBLIC_* value into the JavaScript bundle at build time, so the
value baked into a store binary is whatever the BUILD MACHINE saw. EAS builders do not read
apps/mobile/.env — it is gitignored and never uploaded — so a production build with these
unset ships a bundle pointing at `undefined`, which fails at the first request with an
unhelpful error. The non-secret ones are pinned per profile below; the two that differ per
environment are declared in the EAS project's secrets and referenced by name, so a rotated
key does not require a code change.
None of these are secrets. They are public by design: the anon key is filtered by RLS on
every table, and the publishable key can only create payment methods. The service-role key
and the Stripe secret key are server-side only and appear nowhere in this file.

android.//: serviceAccountKeyPath points at a Play Console service-account JSON kept OUTSIDE the repo. `internal` is the safe default track: it publishes to a named tester list, never to the public listing, so a mis-tagged submit cannot ship to users.

ios.//: ascAppId and appleTeamId are set in the EAS project rather than committed: they are account identifiers, and a fork of this repo submitting to our App Store record would be a genuine problem.
